생활사 박물관의 소규모 전시 포스터 3종을 만들어 주세요. 모두 세로 2:3입니다. 흑백만 쓰되 사진과 그래픽은 사용할 수 있습니다. 오래 쓰며 손에 익은 열쇠와 손잡이를 주제로 한 전시입니다. 열쇠의 마모와 손잡이의 닿는 부분이 주제에 연결되게 해 주세요. 이 물건의 실제 관계가 충분한 크기의 비문자 시각 중심이어야 하고, 글자와 여백이나 작은 기호만으로 끝내지 마세요. 으스스한 범죄물이나 골동품 상점 광고처럼 보이지 않았으면 합니다. 아래 문구를 모두 그대로 넣고, 없는 유물 번호나 연대는 만들지 마세요.

CURRENT EXECUTION SCOPE: Produce exactly ONE independent R7-B07-M3 poster now. The original request's total of three is handled outside this isolated role. The older planning-only sentence in the coordinator constraints is superseded by this current production instruction. Do not print role names, field names, direction explanations or metadata.

Use case: ads-marketing. Asset type: a finished small museum exhibition poster, one single flat opaque rectangular image. Width:height 2:3, portrait. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력. No mockup, frame, wall scene, multi-poster panel, contact sheet or alternate design.

DESIGN SPEC — Two observations of the same familiar door hardware, joined by the title:
Use ONLY black, pure white and neutral grayscale, with no warm or cool tint. Quiet observational museum photography, ordinary daily-life intimacy, clear soft side light. The actual key and lever are the substantial visual content. The contrast between a broad touched grip and a narrow touched key rim should be visible before text is read.

Layout on the single poster: top photograph occupying approximately the upper 32% of height, generous white information area occupying approximately 36%, bottom photograph approximately the lower 32%. The combined photographs take about two thirds of the sheet. They are two independent editorial close views at different magnifications, not a continuous falsely connected perspective scene and not two separate posters. Top and bottom photographs bleed to the sheet edges. Use the same plain matte light-gray door surface and matching ordinary hardware in both photographs. No hands, people, decorative props, artifact numbers, labels, logos or invented inscriptions.

TOP PHOTOGRAPH: A large horizontal lever on a round mounting rosette attached to the door. Place its visible rotation spindle/attachment at the left, with the grip extending right and enough breathing room that the entire useful grip length and end are identifiable. The broad curved front/top surface where fingers and palm repeatedly touch is gently polished, slightly smoother and brighter than the protected area near the mount. A few plausible fine local wear traces may remain at the grip, but avoid blanket scratches, allover rust or uniform distressed texture. The softly lit grip is the first broad shape; the metal reflection follows its curvature. Keep the plate, attachment and actual door contact visible.

CENTRAL WHITE AREA: One coherent left-aligned black type block, ample width and approximately 6% side margins. Every one of the seven supplied strings appears exactly once. Korean letters have natural square proportions, clear counters, coherent weight and ordinary word spacing, never squeezed horizontally. Title near the upper part of the white area at roughly 1.7–2.0 times the subtitle size, substantial but comfortably within one horizontal line. Put the subtitle close beneath it. Give a clear pause, then date and venue as the next group. Give a smaller pause, then opening hours and free admission as the next group. Put the complete unbroken guide URL line last. At the nominal width, reserve room for the full hours string and full URL line in normal proportions. All detail lines should be readable at the usage view, with no tiny footer. The only printed copy, in reading order:
손이 기억하는 물건
열쇠와 손잡이의 생활사
2026.12.08–2027.02.14
생활기억박물관 작은전시실
화–일 10:00–18:00 / 월요일 휴관
관람료 무료
전시 안내 example.org/hand-memory
Use the exact en-dash-like visible marks from the supplied strings in date and hours, retaining all digits and punctuation. Leave distinct white clearance between type and both photograph boundaries. No rules, extra captions or ornaments are needed.

BOTTOM PHOTOGRAPH: A close view of a circular door lock cylinder on the same door, with an ordinary functional key actually inserted into the cylinder keyway. Show the cylinder face, the readable keyway connection, the short exposed blade/neck, and the whole graspable head, at a slight oblique angle so the insertion makes physical sense. The cylinder on the left and the head toward the right/lower-right make the narrow touched perimeter visually distinct. The key head's perimeter and grasped metal have a narrow gently polished edge and a few localized softened wear traces; its recessed center can remain matte. The key's shaft must connect continuously into the keyway, without floating or impossible geometry. No loose keys or keychain. Do not crop down to mere metal texture: the working object and outline remain recognizable. Its reflective rim follows the actual metal edges. The bottom lock is physically below the lever in use; the two close views communicate unlocking and opening the same door.

The white information area connects the upper broad grip wear to the lower narrow key wear. Keep the museum tone humane and matter-of-fact: neutral daylight, clean editorial rhythm, no ominous darkness, spotlight drama, antique dealer styling, sepia, ornate lettering, criminal atmosphere or horror devices.
